contract: Calling l9 .join in the current parent actor waits until pending-children is zero; a join of another task raises /join-of-other-task
Child creation increments parent.pending-children; terminal child completion decrements it after all scope and Task finalizers run and actor cleanup completes
When last pending child completes, a joining parent is resumed via the existing ready queue; spurious wakes do not permit an early join return

When a Task completes while owning descendants, its completed and still-active children are reparented to its grandparent, with weak parent-id updated and active counts transferred before decrementing the finishing task
The reparent walk uses an iterative while/index array traversal. No recursion or per-instruction scheduler overhead was added

join returns the ordered array of completed Task objects, including typed .result/.error and .canceled? state; ownership transfers to the caller. The joining parent clears subtasks, forks and failed-children references
The caller may keep the snapshot for supervision or drop it to release terminal child records; join called again without new children returns an empty array
A canceled parent remains scheduler-eligible while joining so it can collect the final results of canceled children; this does not restart its normal work

If pending children remain but no actor is runnable, join raises /join-no-runnable-child and restores its own joining/paused flags; it does not silently return or busy-poll. This is NOT yet an asynchronous wait for a future external wake-up
